Sorel (left the team in 2025-09)","root_cause":"Connection pool exhaustion. The RDS Proxy idleClientTimeout (300 s) was SHORTER than the idle connection recycling delay of the application pool (600 s). The proxy closed connections the application still believed valid; every request landing on a dead socket failed and consumed a fresh slot, and the pool saturated. AWS documents the opposite rule: the pool must recycle BEFORE the proxy. The RSS growth was a consequence (failing requests held their objects), not the cause. The defect can only show off-peak: under load, no connection stays idle long enough to reach the proxy threshold.
